Ghana, Kenya, and India to help tackle shortfalls in sustainable foreign direct investment (FDI).Our reports Trade and InvestmentSmall Markets, Global Winners: Pathways to Competitive Industries Beyond Trade DistortionsHow can smaller economies build globally competitive industries when they lack the scale and resources to compete in subsidy races or rely on trade barriers? Drawing on five case studies from Indonesia, Peru, Costa Rica, Chile and Viet Nam, Small Markets, Global Winners: Pathways to Competitive Industries Beyond Trade Distortions explains how businesses and governments built export industries that achieved lasting international competitiveness. The paper identifies guiding principles for policy-makers and business leaders working to achieve comparable success. These include overcoming bottlenecks to firm growth, building local capabilities, creating a compelling business case for investment and, critically, sustaining public–private collaboration over time The case studies – which encompass industries from electronic vehicles through agro-exports, aquaculture, precision engineering to IT – offer practical insights into how emerging economies can turn local advantages into internationally competitive industries in an increasingly fragmented global economy.21 October 2026Trade and Investment...Unlocking Azerbaijan’s TradeTech PotentialOver the past few decades, Azerbaijan has built substantial digital and logistics foundations. The next opportunity is to strengthen the enabling conditions that allow these assets to support trade, finance and logistics more effectively. Developed by the World Economic Forum in collaboration with C4IR Azerbaijan (4SİM), operating under the Ministry of Economy of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Unlocking Azerbaijan’s TradeTech Potential assesses the country’s TradeTech ecosystem. The analysis draws on 28 stakeholder consultations across 18 organizations, policy review, international benchmarking and a validation workshop in Baku. The paper identifies three priorities: strengthening legal recognition of digital trade documents, improving interoperability between government platforms and private-sector actors and deepening market coordination, solution development and business adoption. It sets out 10 recommendations, sequenced from immediate actions over the first 12 months to structural reforms over 12–36 months, providing a practical pathway from Azerbaijan’s existing digital foundations towards wider TradeTech adoption.19 October 2026Geographies in Depth...Powering AI at Scale: Optimizing Hyperscale Data Centre Infrastructure in MENAPressure is mounting on MENA countries to rapidly scale hyperscale data centre capacity. Governments and sovereign wealth funds are investing heavily to position MENA as a global digital and AI hub. But building this new generation of energy-intensive facilities will require power systems, cooling capacity and regulatory frameworks to evolve at the same pace. Energy infrastructure is already under strain, and hyperscale data centres add a new layer of pressure. Without coordinated planning, hyperscale expansion risks outpacing the energy and water systems that sustain it. This report presents a practical framework for resilient expansion of hyperscale data centres. 14 October 2026Geographies in Depth...Unlocking Value: AI for Resilient Growth in MENAAs the MENA region navigates a more uncertain global landscape, strengthening economic resilience while sustaining growth has become a central priority. In this context, AI is emerging as a powerful enabler, offering new ways to enhance productivity, optimize resource use and unlock long-term value. This report draws on real-world use cases developed with leading regional institutions and distils these experiences into replicable models and pathways for implementation. While the potential economic contribution of AI is significant for the MENA region, realizing it will depend on overcoming persistent barriers to scale.14 October 2026Global Cooperation...The New Global Security Stakeholders: How Public-Private Cooperation Can Advance Security and StabilityThe New Global Security Stakeholders: How Public-Private Cooperation Can Advance Security and Stability presents strategies for aligning the public and private sectors to safeguard global security.15 September 2026Business...ASEAN Digital Economy Outlook 2026ASEAN is entering a decisive phase in its digital economy journey. Connectivity, digital trade facilitation, cybersecurity and digital payments have strengthened the foundations for regional integration. Yet there is a persistent gap between digital readiness and real-world participation. Firms still face friction when trading, paying, authenticating, signing documents and transferring data across borders. The ASEAN Digital Economy Outlook 2026 examines where these implementation gaps persist and what firms need to participate and grow with confidence. It identifies five priorities for the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) and offers an actionable agenda for turning ASEAN’s digital ambition into inclusive, trusted and seamless cross-border growth.14 September 2026Join our work on regions, trade and geopoliticsWe believe multistakeholder dialogue and cooperation underpin the ability to achieve progress on shared priorities.
